source.title: A pyramid with a Ramsey base is Ramsey
source.version_qualification: Exact arXiv v1 only; no journal-version equivalence or acceptance claimed.

reading.native_text_extraction: Navigation and formula cross-checking only; no OCR.

same_paper_coverage.lemma_2_3: Complete relative compactness application, added explicitly

theorem_2_1.scope: Ordinary finite Cartesian product theorem; original Paper I Theorem 20 on printed p.357.

theorem_2_2.scope: Every finite affinely independent configuration is Ramsey, from Frankl-Rodl Theorem5.1 and Definition2.1.
theorem_2_2.qualification: The elementary super-Ramsey-to-Ramsey pigeonhole implication is explained, but the external simplex proof is not counted.

paper_i.reading_role: Original Proposition4 and Theorem20 interfaces; no complete original-paper proof audit.

frankl_rodl.reading_role: Title/publication and exact Definition2.1/Theorem5.1 input; full theorem proof remains external.

rado_quoted_1951.reading_role: Exact Rado selection theorem quoted as Theorem2; the original 1949 proof is not acquired or reviewed here.

source_precision.issue: The source states finite-witness compactness and cites hypergraph compactness without proving that application.
source_precision.treatment: A complete application of the exact existing Rado selection statement is supplied; Rado itself remains external.
source_precision.classification: compilation expansion, not a source erratum

source_precision.issue: The sentence names P and C, whereas the auxiliary apices to be transported form A.
source_precision.treatment: Embed P and A explicitly in the common R^N, and fully justify the ambient isometry extension.

source_precision.issue: The constructive proof uses a nonempty base and finite witness.
source_precision.treatment: The optional empty-base case is a singleton; all nonempty cases include affine dimension zero.

proof_scope.independent_final_review: Not asserted by this author snapshot.
